title: More Verbs That Work Like Gustar

sections.title: Same pattern, more verbs
sections.content: You know *gustar* from A1 Unit 22: the thing you like is the subject, and the pronoun *me*, *te*, *le*, *nos* or *les* shows who feels it. You know *molestar* from A2 Unit 27 and *sorprender* from B2 Unit 4: when the thing that affects you is what someone else does, the clause after *que* is in the subjunctive (*Me sorprende que vengas*). Here you add more verbs of the same type.

sections.title: Verbs of feeling that work like gustar
rows: Me molesta que... / Me fastidia que...
It bothers me that... / It annoys me that...
Nos preocupa que... / Le asusta que...
It worries us that... / It frightens him or her that...
Les encanta que... / Me entristece que...
They love it that... / It makes me sad that...

sections.title: The verb stays singular
sections.content: The clause after *que* is the subject, so the verb is always third person singular, even when the pronoun is *nos* or *les*: *Nos preocupa que*, not *Nos preocupan que*. A plural noun is different, because then the noun is the subject: *Me preocupan los precios*.

items.spanish: Me molesta que mis vecinos hagan ruido por la noche.
items.english: It bothers me that my neighbours make noise at night.

items.spanish: Nos preocupa que el precio siga subiendo.
items.english: It worries us that the price keeps going up.

items.spanish: Les encanta que los visitantes se queden a cenar.
items.english: They love it that the visitors stay for dinner.
It annoyed me that nobody warned us.

sections.content: As in *Quiero comer* from B2 Unit 4, the same person gets an infinitive: *Me molesta esperar* (I am the one waiting), but *Me molesta que esperes* (you are the one waiting). For a finished event use *haya* from B1 Unit 37 with a participle (*Me preocupa que no hayan llamado*), and after a past verb the imperfect subjunctive, as in *Quería que vinieras* from B1 Unit 38 (*Me molestó que llegaran tarde*).
